images.title: Eczema herpeticum
images.caption: Punched-out erosions and crusted vesicles on eczematous skin. Needs urgent aciclovir; impetiginised eczema gives golden crusts instead.
images.credit: Photo: CDC/Dr. Hudson, PHIL #24351 (public domain)

images.title: Tinea capitis
images.caption: Scaly red patch of hair loss on the scalp of a school-age child; hairs may be broken at the surface (black dots).
images.credit: Photo: CDC/Dr. Lucille K. Georg, PHIL #22272 (public domain)

images.title: Kerion
images.caption: Boggy, swollen, circular scalp lesion with alopecia and pustules: inflammatory tinea capitis.
images.credit: Photo: CDC, PHIL #30138 (phil.cdc.gov)

images.title: Chickenpox (varicella)
images.caption: Vesicular rash with lesions at different stages; infectious until every lesion has crusted over.
images.credit: Photo: CDC/Dr. J.D. Millar, PHIL #25244 (public domain)

images.title: Erythema migrans (Lyme disease)
images.caption: Circular, target-like expanding lesion at the site of a tick or insect bite.
images.credit: Photo: CDC/James Gathany, PHIL #9875 (phil.cdc.gov)

images.title: Intraosseous access site: proximal tibia
images.caption: Flat anteromedial proximal tibia, 1-3 cm (about one finger breadth) below the tibial tuberosity; avoid the growth plate.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Barlow and Ortolani tests (DDH)
images.caption: Baby supine, hip and knee flexed to 90 degrees. Barlow adducts and pushes back to dislocate; Ortolani abducts and lifts forwards to relocate with a clunk.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Erb palsy (waiter's tip)
images.caption: Arm adducted and internally rotated, elbow extended, forearm pronated, wrist flexed (C5-C6). Klumpke (C8-T1) gives a claw hand.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Wolff-Parkinson-White pattern
images.caption: Short PR interval, slurred delta wave at the QRS upstroke and a wide QRS from an accessory pathway; causes SVT.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Perthes disease vs slipped capital femoral epiphysis
images.caption: Perthes: small, flat, dense head with wide joint space. SCFE: epiphysis slips down and back and Klein line misses it.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Atopic eczema
images.caption: Dry, scaly, itchy flexural rash with scratch marks (excoriation).
images.credit: Photo: NIAID, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Herpes simplex vesicles
images.caption: Grouped painful vesicles that ulcerate and crust.
images.credit: Photo: Speifensender, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Herpangina
images.caption: Vesicles and ulcers at the back of the mouth (soft palate, uvula, tonsillar pillars) with no gum involvement.
images.credit: Photo: Sterenau, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Hand, foot and mouth disease
images.caption: Vesicles on the palms and soles (also buttocks) with oral ulcers; coxsackie A16 or enterovirus 71.
images.credit: Photo: KlatschmohnAcker, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome
images.caption: Tender red skin that peels easily (positive Nikolsky sign) with fever; mucosae are spared.
images.credit: Photo: CNX OpenStax, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Tinea corporis (ringworm)
images.caption: Circular scaly lesion with a raised edge and central clearing.
images.credit: Photo: Corina G., public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Port-wine stain
images.caption: Capillary malformation present from birth that grows with the child.
images.credit: Photo: Dr. Wonko, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Cafe-au-lait macules
images.caption: Flat, uniformly pale-brown patches; six or more (over 5 mm before puberty) is one NF1 criterion.
images.credit: Photo: Idiculla J. et al., CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Incontinentia pigmenti
images.caption: Linear streaky lesions along Blaschko lines that go vesicular, then warty, then hyperpigmented.
images.credit: Photo: Kitakawa et al., CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Aplasia cutis congenita
images.caption: Well-demarcated, hairless, membranous skin defect on the scalp vertex of a newborn.
images.credit: Photo: Liwen Xu, Kevin X. Liu, Maryanne M. Senna, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Acanthosis nigricans
images.caption: Rough, dark skin at the back of the neck, a marker of insulin resistance.
images.credit: Photo: Masryyy, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Slapped cheek disease (erythema infectiosum)
images.caption: Bright red cheeks, followed by a lacy reticular rash on the trunk and limbs; parvovirus B19.
images.credit: Photo: Andrew Kerr, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Roseola infantum (exanthem subitum)
images.caption: Pink maculopapular rash on the trunk appearing as a high fever settles in an infant; HHV-6.
images.credit: Photo: Emiliano Burzagli, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Meningococcal septicaemia rash
images.caption: Non-blanching purpuric rash in a febrile, toxic child, sometimes with neck stiffness.
images.credit: Photo: Glei A.I., Shkurba A.V., public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Henoch-Schonlein purpura (IgA vasculitis)
images.caption: Palpable purpura and petechiae over the buttocks and extensor lower limbs.
images.credit: Photo: Profrofrof, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Psoriasis
images.caption: Well-demarcated scaly plaques on knees and elbows, with nail pitting.
images.credit: Photo: Seenms, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Juvenile dermatomyositis
images.caption: Violaceous heliotrope rash around the eyes and Gottron papules.
images.credit: Photo: Dugan E.M. et al., CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Malar rash (SLE)
images.caption: Facial rash over the cheeks and nose in a child with arthritis, cytopenias and positive ANA.
images.credit: Photo: CNX OpenStax, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Kawasaki disease
images.caption: Fever with conjunctivitis, red lips and mucosal changes, rash, extremity changes and a cervical node.
images.credit: Photo: Dong Soo Kim, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Urticaria
images.caption: Itchy raised red wheals over the body, circular in shape.
images.credit: Photo: Enochlau, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Erythema nodosum
images.caption: Tender red nodules on the shins; the commonest skin sign of IBD, especially Crohn disease.
images.credit: Photo: Doc James, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum
images.caption: Injected conjunctivae with copious purulent discharge at day 2-5 of life.
images.credit: Photo: CDC/J. Pledger, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Congenital cataract (rubella)
images.caption: White opacity of the lens with an absent red reflex; part of the congenital rubella picture.
images.credit: Photo: CDC, PHIL #4284, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Preseptal (periorbital) cellulitis
images.caption: Red, swollen eyelids with full, painless eye movements and normal vision.
images.credit: Photo: Afrodriguezg, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Orbital cellulitis
images.caption: Painful, swollen red eye with visual disturbance, pain on eye movement or proptosis.
images.credit: Photo: Jonathan Trobe, MD (Kellogg Eye Center), CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Leukocoria (retinoblastoma until proven otherwise)
images.caption: White pupillary reflex, sometimes with a squint; needs urgent ophthalmology review.
images.credit: Photo: National Cancer Institute, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Amoxicillin rash in EBV infection
images.caption: Rash after amoxicillin in a child with sore throat and lymphadenopathy; not a true allergy.
images.credit: Photo: RainbowKatie, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Gram-negative intracellular diplococci (meningococcus)
images.caption: Gram-negative diplococci seen in CSF; pneumococcus is Gram-positive.
images.credit: Photo: CDC/Dr. Brodsky, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Cryptosporidium oocysts
images.caption: Oocysts on modified Ziehl-Neelsen stain; causes watery diarrhoea and bloating.
images.credit: Photo: CDC DPDx, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Necrotising enterocolitis
images.caption: Abdominal X-ray showing pneumatosis intestinalis (air in the bowel wall); free air under the diaphragm would mean perforation.
images.credit: Photo: Hellerhoff, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Long QT syndrome
images.caption: QT 540 ms with a long, broad T wave versus a normal 360 ms; risk of torsades and exertional syncope.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Supraventricular tachycardia
images.caption: Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at about 270/min with no visible P waves.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Hyperkalaemia ECG changes
images.caption: Peaked T waves, then flat P and wide QRS, then a sine wave before VF or asystole.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Tricyclic overdose: broad QRS
images.caption: QRS widened to 160 ms (normal under 100) from sodium-channel block; treated with IV sodium bicarbonate.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Congenital complete heart block
images.caption: P waves (about 125/min) and QRS (about 55/min) beat independently; maternal anti-Ro/La antibodies.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Normal neonatal ECG
images.caption: Dominant R wave in V1, right axis, and T wave in V1 inverted after the first week.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Hypsarrhythmia (infantile spasms)
images.caption: Chaotic, very high-voltage slow waves with multifocal spikes on EEG.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Tanner stages
images.caption: Breast stages 1-5 and pubic hair stages 1-5; stage 3 breast has no separation of areola from breast contour.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Cranial sutures and craniosynostosis
images.caption: Skull from above showing sutures and fontanelles; early sagittal fusion gives a long narrow head (scaphocephaly) with a palpable ridge.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Cervical lymph node regions
images.caption: Occipital, post-auricular, pre-auricular, submandibular, anterior and posterior cervical and supraclavicular nodes; supraclavicular is always abnormal.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Salter-Harris fractures
images.caption: Types I-V of growth plate fracture (SALTR); type I goes through the physis only and usually heals in a cast.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Osgood-Schlatter disease
images.caption: Painful, tender bony swelling at the tibial tuberosity in an active adolescent; traction apophysitis.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Bell palsy (LMN facial palsy)
images.caption: Whole half of the face weak including the forehead, eye cannot close; UMN lesions spare the forehead.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Retinopathy of prematurity
images.caption: Zones I-III and stages 1-5: demarcation line, ridge, extraretinal fibrovascular proliferation, partial and total detachment.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Intraventricular haemorrhage and PVL
images.caption: Cranial ultrasound drawing of grades I-IV IVH; periventricular leukomalacia shows white-matter cysts beside the ventricles.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Ventricular septal defect
images.caption: Hole in the ventricular septum with left-to-right shunt; pansystolic murmur at the left lower sternal edge.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Patent ductus arteriosus
images.caption: Duct joining the aorta to the pulmonary artery; continuous machinery murmur and bounding pulses.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Atrioventricular septal defect
images.caption: Hole at the centre of the heart with one common AV valve; the typical defect in Down syndrome.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome
images.caption: Tiny left ventricle and aorta with the body supplied through the duct; collapse when the duct closes.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Posterior urethral valves
images.caption: Dilated ureters and kidneys with a thick-walled trabeculated bladder in a boy; confirmed by MCUG.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Trisomies 21, 18 and 13
images.caption: Down: single palmar crease, sandal gap, upslanting eyes. Edwards: overlapping fingers, rocker-bottom foot. Patau: polydactyly, cleft lip and palate.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Tuberous sclerosis
images.caption: Ash-leaf macules, facial angiofibromas, shagreen patch, periungual fibromas and cardiac rhabdomyomas.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: 22q11 deletion (DiGeorge syndrome)
images.caption: CATCH-22: cardiac conotruncal defects, abnormal face, thymic hypoplasia, cleft palate, hypocalcaemia.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Ectopia lentis: Marfan vs homocystinuria
images.caption: Marfan lens dislocates up; homocystinuria lens dislocates down, with learning difficulty and thrombosis.
images.credit: Illustration: Easy Pedia

images.title: Ash-leaf macule (tuberous sclerosis)
images.caption: Hypopigmented leaf-shaped patch in a child with seizures; other skin signs are shagreen patch and angiofibromas.
images.credit: Photo: Portocarrero et al. 2018, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (top: hypopigmented macules; middle: shagreen patch; bottom: periungual fibroma)
